issues.problem: The r1 fix only checks the 'bash <script>' form. A foreign file named silver-bullet run directly by path, or by path inside bash -c, is still accepted as the sanctioned adapter. So is any file whose path ends in /scripts/resolve-instruction-ledger.sh, directly or through bash. The parent can then run arbitrary code that a worker (or anything earlier) placed under one of those names.
issues.evidence: p2-bash.sh (claude parent, directive guard), with $P/evil/silver-bullet and $P/evil/scripts/resolve-instruction-ledger.sh as '#!/bin/bash echo PWNED' scripts and ./silver-bullet in the project: ALLOW '$P/evil/silver-bullet invoke-skill silver'; ALLOW './silver-bullet invoke-skill silver'; ALLOW "bash -c '$P/evil/silver-bullet invoke-skill silver'"; ALLOW '$P/evil/scripts/resolve-instruction-ledger.sh list'; ALLOW 'bash $P/evil/scripts/resolve-instruction-ledger.sh list'. By contrast 'bash $P/evil/silver-bullet invoke-skill silver' is DENY.
issues.suggested_fix: Apply one rule to the program path in every form. A bare name (resolved on PATH) or a path that resolves to the plugin's own scripts/silver-bullet or scripts/resolve-instruction-ledger.sh is accepted; any other path containing '/' is refused, both directly and inside sh -c.

issues.location: hooks/agent-delegation-guard.sh:76-87 (and F2 shell_analysis for git checkout)
issues.problem: The tree-scope check covers only writes with scope 'tree'. 'git restore .' is reported with scope 'path' and path = the repo root (a directory containing the owned dir), so it is not matched. 'git checkout .' and 'git checkout <branch>' get no writes at all from F2 (read_only:false, writes:[]), so the guard allows them even though they overwrite owned files during an active delegation.
issues.evidence: p6-deleg.sh, ownership_scope=[<proj>/src]: ALLOW 'git checkout .', ALLOW 'git checkout -- .', ALLOW 'git restore .', ALLOW 'cd docs && git checkout .' (ok), ALLOW 'git checkout other-branch'. F2 JSON: 'git restore .' => writes:[{path:<repo root>,via:'git restore',scope:'path'}]; 'git checkout .' => writes:[].
issues.suggested_fix: Treat any write whose path is an ancestor directory of an owned path as in scope, whatever its scope. Ask F2 to model git checkout <pathspec>/<branch> as path or tree writes. Until then, deny non-read-only commands with no writes while a delegation is active, or document the gap.

issues.problem: The queue picks required_deploy_devops (which has no tdd) for the silver-devops composer in any project. completion-audit recognises the devops composer only from active_workflow=devops-cycle or a workflow id it can recover (SB_WORKFLOW_ID in the hook env, or an assignment in the command). In a full-dev-cycle project the honest silver-devops queue therefore ends with gh pr create blocked for /tdd. Separately, the silver-deploy and silver-canary queues reach silver-ship without the review triad, so the delivery floor never applies to them and they miss about 10 required_deploy skills.
issues.evidence: p5-pr.sh: template project (full-dev-cycle), feat/x, approval marker, state = every flow_to_skill of the silver-devops queue -> '🛑 COMPLETION BLOCKED — Workflow incomplete ... ❌ /tdd'. p4-queue.sh: silver-deploy is missing silver-quality-gates, silver-review, silver-validate, silver-review-request, silver-review-triage, silver-triage, silver-branch-finish, silver-completion-audit, tdd and verify-tests; silver-canary is similar.
issues.suggested_fix: Key the queue's deploy list the same way deploy-tier.sh does: the devops list only for an active devops-cycle workflow, otherwise required_deploy. Alternatively, have completion-audit read the composer from orchestrator.json. Decide and document whether deploy/canary composers are expected to reach gh pr create or deploy on their own.

issues.location: F2 read-only verdict (hooks/lib/tool-input/shell_analysis.py), consumed by sb_orchestrator_parent_bash_allowed
issues.problem: Cross-package (F2). A PATH= assignment on a read-only command is still read-only, so the parent may run 'PATH=<dir> git status', which executes <dir>/git. F2 already refuses BASH_ENV=, GIT_PAGER= and GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF= on the same path.
issues.evidence: p2-bash.sh: ALLOW 'PATH=$P/evil git status'; DENY 'BASH_ENV=... git status', 'GIT_PAGER=... git log', 'GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF=... git diff'.
issues.suggested_fix: F2: treat PATH= (and other lookup-changing variables) as non-read-only, or allow only a short list of assignments.
